title: The Nvidia CEO Explained
brief: Explain why one chip company became the backbone of the AI boom, what Nvidia’s GPUs actually do, and why Jensen Huang’s sudden departure could matter beyond Wall Street. topic_candidates.title: I Fixed A Broken Fold Phone
topic_candidates.query: iPhone Duo foldable phone hinge screen repairability iFixit 2026
topic_candidates.brief: Use the viral dead-fold-phone repair format to explain why foldable phones fail at the hinge and why a phone can be more repairable overall while its inner screen remains extremely expensive to replace. Show the sequence: flexible OLED, layered screen materials, hinge movement, dust ingress, stress concentration, then the real-world repair bill. Keep it product-independent rather than reviewing one brand.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: iFixit’s teardown found that the iPhone Duo uses linked joints, gears, springs and a flexible cable to manage bending, but reported that dust can reach the hinge and that inner-display replacement costs $999 out of warranty. It gave the device a provisional 5/10 repairability score—the highest iFixit has given a foldable, but still difficult to repair. ([ifixit.com](https://www.ifixit.com/News/119895/iphone-duo-teardown?utm_source=openai))
topic_candidates.broke_on: November 14–16, 2026 breakout from Tech By Aadil titled “I Fixed A Dead Fold Phone,” with a 5.4× channel-average breakout, plus adjacent crease and hinge videos in the same list.
topic_candidates.science_angle: Materials fatigue and mechanical stress: repeated bending stretches the outer layers of a display more than the inner layers, while hinges must distribute force without creating a sharp stress hotspot.

topic_candidates.title: 2.4Ghz vs 5Ghz vs 6Ghz Wi-Fi Explained!
topic_candidates.query: 2.4 GHz vs 5 GHz vs 6 GHz Wi-Fi speed range interference official explanation
topic_candidates.brief: Explain which Wi-Fi band ordinary people should use in a crowded home: 2.4 GHz travels farther through walls but is slower and more crowded; 5 GHz is faster at shorter range; 6 GHz can be the cleanest and fastest option nearby but has the shortest practical reach and needs compatible devices. The payoff is a simple rule for choosing the right band instead of treating the labels as marketing.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: Google’s official Wi-Fi documentation describes 2.4 GHz, 5 GHz and 6 GHz as separate wireless bands that may appear as separate networks and require users to choose among them on some routers. The video can explain the trade-offs without claiming that one band is always best. ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/googlehome/answer/6293481/2-4-%E3%81%8A%E3%82%88%E3%81%B3-5-ghz-%E5%B8%AF%E3%81%A7%E3%81%AE-google-nest-wifi-%E3%81%A8-google-wifi-%E3%81%AE%E5%8B%95%E4%BD%9C?utm_source=openai))
topic_candidates.broke_on: November 15–16, 2026 breakout from Makhir titled “2.4Ghz vs 5Ghz vs 6Ghz Wifi!”, a highly educational short with strong current views-per-hour.
topic_candidates.science_angle: Radio propagation and interference: lower-frequency 2.4 GHz signals generally penetrate obstacles better, while wider and newer bands can provide more capacity but lose usable range more quickly.

topic_candidates.title: Windows Is Saving Your Screen
topic_candidates.query: Microsoft Windows Recall screenshots local storage privacy official 2026
topic_candidates.brief: Turn the alarming “Windows is sending your files” idea into a clear explanation of what Recall actually does. Show that the feature can periodically save screenshots of activity, index them locally for search, require Windows Hello, and allow users to pause, delete or filter snapshots. Then explain the important distinction: local storage reduces cloud exposure, but a searchable record of your screen is still sensitive if someone gains access to the device.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: Microsoft says Recall is opt-in, saves snapshots of the active screen periodically, stores and processes them locally on Copilot+ PCs, encrypts the data, and lets users pause or delete snapshots. Microsoft also warns that filtering does not stop websites, ISPs or organizations from knowing that a site was accessed. ([support.microsoft.com](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/privacy/privacy-and-control-over-your-recall-experience?utm_source=openai))
topic_candidates.broke_on: November 15–16, 2026 breakout from Zack Shutt titled “Windows Is Sending Your Files To Microsoft,” indicating strong audience interest in the privacy implications of AI features built into everyday computers.
topic_candidates.science_angle: On-device AI and information security: Recall converts screenshots into searchable representations on the PC, while encryption and Windows Hello are intended to control who can unlock that data.
